gap_claims.original_text: Local o tokens reset each frame; A and X are not simultaneously labeled. Continuity inferred from nearest-neighbor positions over consecutive frames, not from persistent tracker identity. No missing-frame interpolation is used.

Large temporal gap between the A-labelled early frames (G006-G009) and X-labelled late frames (G032-G034) is filled with unlabeled observations. Local tokens reset each frame, so A and X are not persistent identities. Matching only by proximity would require unobserved identity continuity; no interpolation is permitted.

The ~5.4 s gap contains many anonymous observations; neither A nor Y has a persistent token chain. Any A-Y association would need to assume a turn and crossing through unlabeled fish, which is not directly observed.

No intermediate observation labels B or X. The gap and multiple crossing fish mean that a B-to-X path would require an inferred leftward/upward turn, while a B-to-Y path would require an inferred rightward continuation. Neither is directly observed.

The apparent B-Y compatibility is based on relative position and motion tendency, not on persistent identity. Because many similarly moving unlabeled fish exist in the gap, B-Y cannot be isolated as the only possible association.

A is labeled only at G001; the alternative A-X would require the A trajectory to switch to the X chain at some unobserved/merged interval, which is not supported by the observed frames.

A is labeled only at G001; the bridge to Y relies on unlabeled observations (f005:o02, f015:o02, f025:o02, f029:o03) that form a continuous positional path. There is no labeled persistent identity across the gap.

The B label is present only in G002-G004; after that, identity is inferred from the continuous observed path through G020, G029, and G033. There is a long temporal gap, so support depends on no crossing/identity swap in the intermediate frames.

B is labeled only in G002-G004; the later identity is inferred from unlabeled positional continuity through intermediate frames. Even allowing that gap, the observed B path moves left/down and aligns with X, while Y is the trajectory coming from A.

A's track is followed by nearest-neighbor continuity from G001:o02 through G028:o02 and G029:o03 to Y. The assignment to X would require ignoring that observed continuity. No persistent identity across gaps is assumed.

The local token index resets each frame, but the A-associated track is continuous under nearest-neighbor motion through the sequence. No missing-frame interpolation is used beyond observed continuity.

No missing frames were treated as continuously visible; linking relies on nearest-position continuity from G006/G009 through G032. Local observation tokens reset every frame, so identity is inferred only from observed motion, not token index. Assumes no unobserved identity swap in dense frames.

No missing frames; local tokens are not persistent identities, so edges are inferred from observed motion continuity. Assumes no unobserved crossing after G014 and no identity swap during dense schooling.

No frames were treated as continuously visible across missing observations; all included times are real G frames. Identity inference assumes the nearest observed continuation is the same fish, with no token-index persistence.
A is labeled only in G001-G002; later links use nearest-observation continuity, not persistent identity. The long gap and frame-reset tokens mean no unobserved path is assumed.
A has no labeled late observation; Y is late. The gap is ~3.4 s with frame-reset tokens, so only observed nearest-continuity is used; no interpolation across missing frames is assumed.
B is labeled in G016-G020; linkage to X uses nearest-observation continuity through intermediate frames, not persistent tokens. No missing observations are interpolated.

Large temporal gap between A labels (-2.065 s) and X labels (-0.466 s); intermediates are observed, but no single unbroken labeled track spans the gap. Identity inference relies on observed frame-to-frame continuity, not on persistent frame tokens.

Anonymous endpoint labels are linked by observed nearest-neighbour continuity across frames; no hidden interpolation or tracker identity edit is used. The gap between early B labels and late X labels contains many unlabelled observations, but the observed sequence bridges them.
The only connection is across a 5.5 s unobserved gap (-5.964 s to -0.466 s); no continuous visibility. The comparison uses local observations, not persistent identity.
There is still an unobserved interval; the support is directional rather than a continuous track. No interpolation of missing observations is used.
B's early velocity is very small, so its heading is weakly constrained; a long unobserved gap could hide a large leftward/downward excursion. No continuous visibility is inferred.
The large temporal gap prevents testing continuity; B's early velocity is weak, and Y's late motion is from a different part of the scene. No physical interaction is observed.

No frame contains both A and X. Gap is about 3.23 s between A's last observation (G002 at -3.699 s) and X's first observation (G032 at -0.467 s). No interpolation or continuous visibility is assumed; a turn and unobserved intermediate positions are possible.

No frame contains both A and Y. Gap is about 3.23 s. No interpolation; identity would require unobserved direction change because A's last motion is upward while the direct A-to-Y displacement is downward/rightward.

No frame contains both B and X. Gap is about 1.37 s between B's last observation (G020 at -1.833 s) and X's first observation (G032 at -0.467 s). No continuous visibility across missing frames is assumed; B would need a vertical reversal to link to X.

No frame contains both B and Y. Gap is about 1.37 s. No interpolation is allowed; B's last motion is left/up and Y's first observed motion is right/up, so a turn and large horizontal displacement would be required.

There is no continuous visibility across the long G015-G032 gap. The association is judged only from the labelled endpoint observations and relative spatial/motion ordering, not from interpolated tracks.

No frame-by-frame track is visible across all intermediate frames. The support rests on relative ordering and compatible endpoint motions, not on assumed continuous visibility through missing observations.
The link is inferred from observed directional consistency and relative position across a missing middle interval; it does not assume persistent visibility across unobserved frames.
No continuous tracker identity is available across the missing frames. The contradiction is based on observed endpoint directions and relative positions, not on inferred tracks.

Large temporal gap with no intermediate observations. A's final short segment (G014->G015) was left/down, so A-X would require an unobserved upward turn; the net observed A displacement is opposite X.

Large temporal gap with no continuity. A's final segment was left/down, so this support is based on A's net observed displacement and Y's sustained right/down motion, not on an observed connecting path.

Large temporal gap between G011 and G032 (~2.67 s) with no intermediate observations; no continuous visibility and no interpolation. The support is based only on observed endpoint motion in the separated sequences, not on a tracked path.
Large gap G011-G032 means an unobserved reversal cannot be formally excluded, but observed B and Y motions oppose in both horizontal and vertical components.

Gap from G019 (-2.065 s) to G033 (-0.466 s) is 1.599 s with no intermediate frames. No direct A-to-X visibility is observed; the association would require A to leave its stable right-side position, cross the left-side B track, and reverse vertical motion without interaction evidence.

Gap from G019 (-2.065 s) to G033 (-0.466 s) has no intermediate observations. Support is based on relative motion/position across the gap, not on direct continuity: A is the right-side early fish, Y is the right-side late fish, and the A/B vs X/Y left-right ordering is preserved. The vertical displacement is assumed to result from unsampled motion/turning.

The same 1.599 s unobserved interval separates B and X. Support relies on relative motion: B is the left-side early endpoint and X the left-side late endpoint; B's upward velocity and left-side position are compatible with X's first appearance. The turn to down-right after G033 is an inferred temporal turn, not directly observed.

The gap G019-G033 has no intermediate frames. B-Y would require B to move from left to right and to reverse its observed upward component while A remains right-side; this is an unobserved crossing with no interaction evidence.

No persistent identity is assumed; A lacks verified observations after G002, so the contradiction uses A's observed initial motion plus the presence of a competing B-to-X track. No interpolation across missing frames is used to fill A's path.

No identity swapping is assumed. Y's earlier path is recovered only by local nearest-neighbor continuity and is not itself an end-point label before G032, but the simultaneous G001/G002 observations make A-Y incompatible without an unobserved identity switch.

Assumes local continuity between adjacent observed frames; no interpolation across missing observations is used to bridge B and X. Token indices reset every frame and are not treated as persistent identities.
Relies on observed B-track continuation through unlabeled detections; local tokens are not persistent, and no cross-gap interpolation is used.

A has no labeled observation after -3.699, leaving a gap of about 3.23 s before X. The local frame tokens reset every frame and are not persistent identities; many unlabeled fish are present in each frame, so missing continuity cannot be assumed.

A is unobserved after -3.699; Y is unobserved until -0.467. The gap is about 3.23 s. Without persistent IDs, multiple possible tracks could link A to Y, so this edge cannot be resolved from the available observations.

B is labeled only through G020, and X is labeled from G032 onward; the intervening frames are used by nearest-neighbor continuity, not by persistent tokens. The gap from G020 to G032 is about 1.37 s but is densely sampled by intermediate G frames.

B is unobserved after G020 and Y is unobserved before G032, but B's observed intermediate frames G021-G031 provide a coherent continuation toward X. A B-Y link would require an unobserved turn against the observed relative motion.

Identity through intermediate frames is inferred by nearest-neighbour continuity, not persistent local tokens. At G023 A is assigned to f023:o03 rather than f023:o04; this is based on A's incoming velocity from f022:o04 and the subsequent continuation through f024:o03 and f025:o02. No missing-frame gap exceeds about 0.13 s.

Proximity alone would allow B-X, but the observed B velocity change from G022 to G023 makes the B-X assignment require an unobserved sharp turn. The nearest-neighbour path using f023:o02 continues smoothly to Y.

Assumes nearest-neighbour continuity across consecutive G frames, with the G023 assignment resolved by B's incoming horizontal/vertical velocity. Local tokens are not persistent; no colour, size, or single-frame static cue was used. No missing-frame gap greater than about 0.13 s.

There is a 1.1 second gap between G004 and G005, and local tokens reset each frame; identity continuity is inferred only by nearest-neighbor motion across observed frames, not by persistence of tokens.

No missing frames; token indices reset after G028. A-X contradiction assumes observed nearest-neighbor continuity from G001 o02 through G028 o02 to G029 o03; even if token linking is imperfect, X and A/Y are simultaneous at G029/G033.
Assumes B's right-side lineage continues; observed B-like track never reaches Y's lower-middle position; identity would require unobserved merging.

Local tokens reset every frame; f014:o03, f019:o04, etc. are observations, not persistent tracker identities. Continuity is inferred from successive frame centroids/areas; no unobserved frames are interpolated. The main gap is between labeled A and labeled X.
Local tokens reset; no persistent identity. Contradiction uses observed motion/area and does not assume continuous visibility across missing frames. Intermediate observations instead connect B to Y.

Local tokens reset; no persistent identity. Continuity inferred from successive centroids and area; no interpolation across unobserved frames. Gap between labeled B and labeled Y is spanned by observed intermediate frames.
